_note: Domain events and their subscriber scripts. Lifecycle wiring lives in .claude/settings.json; this file documents intent. Scripts read their payload via _hooklib.load_payload(), so both Claude Code (stdin) and a hand-set HOOK_PAYLOAD work. Every hook here ACTS or DENIES. Hooks whose only output was the name of a skill were deleted on 2026-08-04: hooks and skills are independent, a hook cannot invoke a skill, and a skill name written into hook source is an unvalidated second copy of a routing decision. Skills trigger from their own `description:` frontmatter. Family names match the Notion 'Agentic Workflows (IDE)' target architecture's 10 hook families (decisions/2026-08-21-notion-architecture-merge.md) as of 2026-08-21 -- renamed from the prior session-start/user-prompt/post-run/pre-commit/pre-deploy/on-artifact-create/pre-run/post-tool shape, same mechanisms.

session-init.description: At session start; loads knowledge-doc pointers into context and reports scaffolding/env drift, then measures the repo against the branch point and renders the matching [state:<key>] block from workflow.md. Names no skill -- workflow.md owns what a state means.

prompt-intake.description: Before a turn begins; records this turn's start timestamp for telemetry/09-telemetry.py's turn_latency_seconds, then classifies the prompt's entry shape -- work named with a settled approach, work named with an open one, or neither -- and renders the matching [state:<key>] block from workflow.md. Names no skill: it measures prompt shape, workflow.md's Entry table owns what that shape routes to. A hook cannot invoke a skill, so this raises the entry rule's visibility and does not guarantee a handoff.

stop-finalization.description: After a turn completes; snapshots recovery state, commits the turn as a wip checkpoint if the artefact gates pass, records the unit's state and says so when the chain stops advancing, then runs telemetry/09-telemetry.py as its last step -- kept in this same sequenced dispatch rather than a second, separately registered Stop hook, because the finalizers and the telemetry snapshot share recovery/git state and Claude Code may run separately registered Stop hooks concurrently.

stop-finalization-steps.description: The ordered Stop finalizers called by stop-finalization/00-dispatch.py; manual-only registry entries prevent them being mistaken for independently concurrent Claude hooks
stop-finalization-steps._note: These scripts share recovery and git state and are intentionally not registered as separate Claude Stop hooks. Run the dispatcher, or invoke an individual script only for diagnosis.

telemetry.description: The per-run telemetry snapshot (Notion §21) -- run_id/execution_level/skills_loaded/agents_spawned/etc. Its own family per the Notion target, but still dispatched from stop-finalization/00-dispatch.py's sequence rather than a second Stop registration -- see that family's description for why.

permission-security.description: Before a git commit/push, or a cloud-CLI command, finalizes; refuses credentials, protected-branch commits, AI attribution in either the message or the target repo's configured author, and non-free-tier cloud spend. Dispatched as one in-process script (00-dispatch.py) rather than 4 separate Python launches -- measured on the build machine: 5 PreToolUse processes at 790.8ms avg fell to 2 at 288.1ms avg for the same Bash call, once this and pre-tool/01-halt-guard.py are the only two left. Every check still runs to completion even after an earlier one denies, matching the exact combine-and-deny semantics the 4 separate hook registrations had.

permission-security-checks.description: The 4 checks called in-process by permission-security/00-dispatch.py; each also runs standalone for diagnosis (HOOK_PAYLOAD=... python <path>), same as before the merge.
permission-security-checks._note: Not separately registered in settings.json -- see permission-security's own description for why merging them was worth doing.

pre-edit.description: Before a file write; refuses generated, vendored and lockfile targets

post-edit-validation.description: After a hook script is edited; demands it be fired against a real payload before being trusted

pre-tool.description: Before any tool that changes state or spawns work; refuses while a halt is in force. Reads stay allowed on purpose, so a halt can be investigated

context-budget.description: After a shell tool returns: reports what its input added to permanent session context, names a call this session already made with the same inputs. After a Skill tool call: counts the invocation and the loaded SKILL.md's byte size into a running total tools/bench.py reports. Reports only -- never blocks; a PreToolUse gate on this class of signal was tried once and rejected (see the 2026-08-20 Notion-objectives audit, Gap B).

post-tool.description: After a Read tool call: counts Read-file bytes added to context. After a Task (agent-spawn) dispatch: counts it. After every tool call (matcher "*"): counts it into a total-calls tally, by tool name. After AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode: counts a human-gate firing, by tool name. Separate matchers per script, because each PostToolUse script costs a spawn on every matching call. Reports only -- never blocks. Names no skill in what it emits, per decisions/2026-08-04-hooks-never-name-a-skill.md -- writes to a state file, never to stdout in the normal case
